abstract: Biochemical coupling can change the expression levels and timing predicted by an incoherent feedforward loop (IFFL) model without changing cumulative dose ordering. We derive ordering conditions using shared-production identities and Metzler comparison bounds, with tail guarantees beyond finite computation. A nonlinear example exhibits delayed slope reversal at a fixed dose, on an $O(1/η)$ timescale as pathway mismatch $η$ vanishes. At one fixed joint fit, validated bounds establish decreasing cumulative output across 20-100 ng nominal burden, from zero to full target loading, at every positive finite observation time for a translation-blocking model and an RNA-decay model. Full loading at 20 ng reduces 48-hour cumulative output by 13.35% and 10.18%, respectively, while endpoint concentration in the first model changes by only +0.15%. Preserved ordering therefore does not ensure quantitative agreement.
